<style>
/* The theme sets .reveal p directly (obis_theme.scss:71), and a directly
   matching declaration beats an inherited one, so these rules have to reach the
   element itself rather than style the wrapper. Sizes are px to match the theme,
   which works in px throughout; the blue is the theme's own body colour. */
.reveal .obis-numbers {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
  gap: 1.1em 1.4em;
  background: #C6D9E3;
  padding: 0.9em 1.2em;
  border-radius: 6px;
}
.reveal .obis-numbers p {
  margin: 0;
}
.reveal .obis-stat-value {
  display: block;
  font-size: 50px;
  font-weight: 800;
  line-height: 1.05;
  letter-spacing: -0.01em;
}
.reveal .obis-stat-label {
  display: block;
  font-size: 15px;
  line-height: 1.2;
  margin-top: 0.15em;
}
.reveal .obis-numbers-source p {
  margin-top: 0.6em;
  font-size: 14px;
  color: #545556;
}
/* The numbers are the content here, so let them stack rather than shrink. */
@media (max-width: 800px) {
  .reveal .obis-numbers { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); }
}
</style>

::: {.notes}
These figures are not typed into the slide. scripts/fetch-obis-stats.R pulls
them from api.obis.org and writes _variables.yml, which the slide reads through
the var shortcode. Rerun it before a workshop and the slide updates itself; the
retrieval date underneath is there so the audience knows how current they are.

Datasets is shown exactly rather than rounded, because 6,917 is a number people
recognise and "7K" is not. The node count excludes the OBIS Secretariat, which
coordinates rather than publishes.
:::
